In this issue of Blood Advances, Reddy et al1 deliver a timely message that the cure for transfusion-dependent thalassemia (TDT) in children can be made safer, simpler, and more accessible if transplant programs are built around disciplined protocols, essential medicines, and local capacity.

For decades, matched sibling donor (MSD) bone marrow transplant (BMT) has been an established cure for TDT. However, challenges remain, especially in regions where access to health care and BMT is limited. Thalassemia is common across South Asia and the Middle East, where access to lifelong transfusions, iron chelation, and monitoring can strain families and health systems.
